title: The Kharijites
hookLine: a group rejects the arbitration, declares others unbelievers, and fights Ali

cards: No judgment but God's. In Arabic, la hukma illa lillah. On their face, those are words nobody in Ali's camp would argue with.
But a group of his own soldiers starts shouting them at him: you let men judge between you and Mu'awiyah, and judgment belongs to God alone.
Some of them, the histories note, were among those who had pushed him to accept the talks in the first place. Now they walk out of his camp and set up their own.

teach.b: Kharijites, in Arabic khawarij: those who went out.

teach.h: A WORD OF TRUTH, FOR FALSEHOOD.
teach.b: Ali's answer to their slogan is kept in Sahih Muslim: a word of truth, by which falsehood is intended. The words were true; what they were used for was not.
The Kharijites came to hold that anyone who accepted the arbitration had committed a grave sin and was no longer a believer. Ali, they said, had left Islam, and so had anyone who stood with him.
Once someone is declared an unbeliever, the histories show how quickly the next step comes. Reports say they killed Muslims on the road who would not condemn Ali.
Ali first sent his cousin Ibn Abbas to reason with them, and the reports say some came back. The rest he fought at Nahrawan. The Prophet had warned about this long before.

teach.h: THE WORD RETURNS TO ONE OF THE TWO.
teach.b: Bukhari records him saying that if a person calls his brother an unbeliever, the word returns to one of the two of them: the charge can land on the one who makes it.

Bukhari and Muslim also report the Prophet describing people who would recite the Qur'an without it going past their throats, and Muslim's collection sets that warning beside Ali and the men he faced.
A note of fairness: Ibadi Muslims, in Oman and elsewhere, trace part of their history to early dissenters of this time, but they reject the name Kharijite and the extremes it stands for.
The lesson the tradition draws is about a single move: declaring.

how: Muslim teachers often use the Kharijites as a warning against takfir, declaring other Muslims unbelievers, and cite the hadith that the charge returns to one of the two.

o: Ali's loyal guard, who stayed with him to the end
those who went out from Ali's camp over the arbitration
the judges chosen to settle Siffin by the Qur'an

s: Ali called it a word of truth, used for a falsehood.
calling a fellow Muslim an unbeliever can rebound on the speaker
Bukhari records the Prophet saying the word returns to one of the two.
they trace part of their history to early dissenters but reject the name.

games.q: you're Ali. a group of your own men has walked out, shouting that you've left Islam. what do you do first?
o: send Ibn Abbas to reason with them.
games.why: the reports say he sent Ibn Abbas first, and some came back; he fought the rest at Nahrawan.

practice: Think of the labels people reach for to put someone outside: fake, sellout, not a real one, not one of us.
If there's someone you've quietly placed outside the circle, hand the verdict back; you can still disagree with them completely. If you pray, you can leave the judgment with God.

wordCard.voice: The Kharijites. Those who went out: soldiers who left Ali over the arbitration, declared other Muslims unbelievers, and fought him at Nahrawan. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: those who went out, the name given to the group that left Ali's camp.

carryVoice: Your line: not our place to declare. Disagreement doesn't need a verdict on anyone. Until tomorrow.
